answers.implementation_then_now: No change was found. Art. 11 of Ley 1155 still carries the 1991 annotation and nothing later, and the only reform in the window (Ley 10508, Aug. 2024) touched arts. 15 and 18, not the renunciation clause. In practice the TSE Civil Registry naturalised people at a high, steady rate through the period: 6,277 letters of naturalisation in 2023 and 5,541 in 2024, according to the Registry director as reported by La Nación (July 2025). The same report says Nicaragua's 2025 constitutional reform ends dual nationality for Nicaraguans who naturalise abroad. That is a change in foreign law, not Costa Rican law, though it may lower demand. No reports were found of the renunciation clause being applied unevenly, so the rating stays 'Usually' on both dates. This rests on evidence about naturalisation volume, not on how the renunciation declaration itself is handled.

answers.implementation_then_now: 2023: Decree 43809-MGP had been published (Dec. 2022), and its window ran from 1 March 2023 to 29 Feb. 2024. It regularised 10,551 rejected or pending asylum applicants from Nicaragua, Venezuela and Cuba (DGME data), with DGME formally delegating case decisions in June 2023. This is real but time-limited and nationality-limited, so 'Sometimes'. 2026: on 1 January 2026 no extraordinary window was open. The window had closed in Feb. 2024, and in April 2025 DGME said it would not reopen the category under the Chaves government. Only renewals and the ordinary routes (e.g. marriage, art. 73) remained, against an asylum backlog of about 178,000 (UNHCR end-2025). Practice therefore dropped to 'Rarely; Sometimes'. The 2026 Complementary Category (DG-0064-05-2026, May 2026, applications from Sept. 2026) explains why the starting answer of Nov. 2026 is back at 'Sometimes'. No practice data was found on the agricultural special category (Decree 44281 of Nov. 2023).

answers.starting_answer_concern: The 'Yes' rests mainly on general policy clauses (arts. 6(1), 7(6)) and the discretionary power in art. 93, plus time-limited decrees and resolutions. There is no standing statutory right of irregular workers to regularise, and the coder admits as much. DG-0064-05-2026 is cited only through the press.
answers.notes: The protection answer is Yes on both dates because the statutory basis (arts. 6(1), 7(6), 93, 94, 73) did not change in substance. The change is in implementation only, a documented shift: the 43809 window closed in Feb. 2024 and DGME refused to reopen it in 2025. The CETC 2026 resolution post-dates 1 Jan 2026, so it does not count for that date.

events.instrument: Ley N.º 10508, Reforma de los artículos 15 y 18 de la Ley 1155, Ley de Opciones y Naturalizaciones (Alcance 147, La Gaceta 158)
events.what_changed: New art. 15(4) bars naturalisation for anyone convicted of an intentional offence carrying more than three years' imprisonment within the last ten years. It exempts persons declared stateless whose earlier convictions the Foreign Ministry knew of when it made the declaration. This bears only on stateless adults born abroad who naturalise. The core guarantee (Const. art. 13(3)-(4), Ley 1155 art. 10) is untouched.
events.passage: b. Las personas extranjeras apátridas que cuenten con antecedentes penales previos a la declaratoria de dicha condición por parte del Ministerio de Relaciones Exteriores, siempre que al momento de la declaratoria el citado Ministerio tenga conocimiento de la condena y a pesar de ello haya declarado la condición de apátrida a su favor obviando tal condena.

answers.implementation_then_now: The constitutional option of registering children born in Costa Rica to foreign parents, and nationality for foundlings, operated unchanged on both dates through the TSE Civil Registry. UNHCR documents the TSE's statelessness work, including the 2018 naturalisation of a recognised stateless person and the Chiriticos late-registration project with Panama for cross-border Ngäbe children (UNHCR 2018). For the later period, UNHCR Costa Rica reports 495 persons at risk of statelessness on 31 Dec. 2025, a small residual caseload. That points to gaps in birth registration rather than refusals of nationality. No documented change in practice between 2023 and 2026 was found, so 'Usually' holds on both dates. Evidence on the 2023-2025 period is thin.

answers.starting_answer_concern: The starting citation says Ley 1155 'waives the criminal-record bar to naturalisation for persons declared stateless'. That waiver exists only since Ley 10508 entered into force on 28 Aug. 2024 (art. 15(4)(b)), and it covers only the new art. 15(4) bar for convictions the Foreign Ministry knew of at the declaration. It was not law on 1 Jan. 2023, and the older art. 11(4) good-conduct requirement still applies. Separately, art. 13(3) is an option that depends on registration, not automatic attribution, and stateless adults born abroad must still naturalise, so the 'Yes' is generous.
answers.notes: The Ley 10508 amendment is recorded but does not change the indicator answer, because the 'Yes' rests on Const. art. 13(3)-(4) and Ley 1155 art. 10, both unchanged. Treaty basis: the 1961 Convention, directly applicable under Const. art. 7.
